newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper called to open slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper called to open slightly lower.

text.p: COMEX copper futures were called to open slightly lower Tuesday in line with LME copper as the market corrects Monday's late gains.
COMEX July copper was called unchanged to down 0.50 cent from Monday's close of 122.20 cents a lb after trading from 122.10 to 121.75 cents on ACCESS.
LME warehouse copper stocks fell a further 1,550 tonnes to 122,225 tonnes in Tuesday's data, while COMEX copper stocks were up 2,068 short tons at 48,710 short tons Monday.
LME copper stocks have fallen steadily from 145,750 tonnes at the start of May and from around 200,000 tonnes at the start of the year, reflecting a tightening supply situation, analysts said.

COMEX stocks have been rising recently as LME stocks have fallen, but not all the COMEX stock rise could be attributed to arbitrage-related shipments from LME warehouses, and could also be indicative of the surge in copper imports into the U.S. while exports have fallen, analysts said.
Shipment delays still hinder Ok Tedi mine in Papua New Guinea, while the strike at Inco Limited in Canada continued into its third week.
